perspectives.name: discovery-weak-signals

factors.name: revenueDiversification
factors.basis: Serve reported Q2 2026 revenue of $3.2 million, up 404% year over year, with recurring revenue above 50% of total and DoorDash-derived revenue up nearly 50% sequentially.

risks: The company cut full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $9-$10 million because Uber Eats delivery volume was below expectations and projected second-half demand was removed.
contradictions: Strong year-over-year growth and improving recurring mix coexist with a material reduction in full-year revenue expectations.
unknowns: Durability of DoorDash growth and pace of replacement for lost Uber Eats volume remain unknown.

perspectives.name: expectations-execution

factors.name: executionAgainstGuidance
factors.basis: Q2 execution showed rapid growth and $240.4 million liquidity, but management revised 2026 revenue guidance down to $9-$10 million while reducing non-GAAP operating expense guidance to $140-$150 million.

risks: Lower delivery volume through Uber Eats demonstrates customer/channel concentration and demand-conversion risk.
contradictions: Operating expense guidance improved while revenue guidance deteriorated.
unknowns: Whether new Grubhub and other verticals can offset the removed Uber Eats demand within the current planning horizon is not established.

sources.origin: Serve Robotics Investor Relations / Q2 2026 results
facts: Q2 revenue was $3.2 million, up 404% year over year and 9% sequentially.
Recurring revenue exceeded 50% of total revenue and DoorDash-derived revenue grew nearly 50% sequentially.
FY2026 revenue guidance was revised to $9-$10 million due to lower-than-expected Uber Eats delivery volume and removal of projected second-half demand.
FY2026 non-GAAP operating expense guidance improved to $140-$150 million.

result: Primary Q2 execution evidence adds a decision-useful guidance contradiction and liquidity context for Alpha; numeric scoring remains Alpha-owned.
